answer: A reputation bond works like a thread that ties each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history: before an agent can trade, it must stake a deposit and build a record of fulfilled contracts, each attested by counterparties. A sybil attacker would have to fund and age every fake identity separately, like raising a whole flock of ravens one bird at a time, while honest agents keep a single ivory-clean record. Forging many identities then costs more than any gain from gaming the market.
